podcast.body: Released in 1978, this song features one of the most iconic saxophone riffs, played by Rafael Ravenscroft, although the prevailing view is that Rafferty himself composed the riff after experimenting with guitar and piano. Rafferty chose the saxophone as it evoked the "jazz period of New York City," specifically referencing 1920s jazz. The lyrics were written during a period of personal turmoil, reflecting his struggles with alcoholism, bipolar disorder, depression, and legal issues with his Stealers Wheel contract (1975-1978), portraying a desire for escape and a sober life, but acknowledging a persistent restlessness. The song reached number 2 on the Billboard Hot 100, where it remained for six weeks due to alleged label interference. "Rafferty said that he tried the guitar and the piano for that riff instead of the saxophone But set him on the sax because he boked the feeling that he wanted The feeling he wanted was the jazz period of New York City And I think by that he means the jazz period of the 1920s"
